subject: SLO cadence & degradation margin (p50/p95) — Nimbus Health
messages:
From: Danielle Ortiz <dani.ortiz@nimbushealth.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Cc: Nimbus Health SRE <sre@nimbushealth.com>
Date: 2025-05-12T09:14:00-07:00
Subject: SLO cadence & degradation margin (p50/p95) — Nimbus Health

Hi Karthik,

Thanks again for the demo last week. As we prepare the commercial addendum, the engineering team surfaced a question about how Redwood measures the p50/p95 latency commitments for the Hosted API. Our concern: a single large batch or regional burst could push the rolling window numbers into violation even if tail latency is otherwise good.

Specifically, can you confirm:
- Whether p50/p95 are computed on a rolling 30-day window or on discrete epochs (e.g., daily/12hr) for contractual SLA purposes.
- If you support transient carveouts for short-lived bursts above a defined TPS threshold.
- How credit calculations would treat a short outage that affects p95 for one day but not long-term trends.

We want to avoid an outcome where a seasonal surge incorrectly triggers SLA credits. If there are options (rolling window vs epoch-based measurement, transient degradation margin), please outline the operational and legal implications.

Thanks — we need this for our legal and SRE review.

— Danielle Ortiz
Sr. Manager, Platform Engineering
Nimbus Health

Attachment: None

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
To: Danielle Ortiz <dani.ortiz@nimbushealth.com>
Cc: Nimbus Health SRE <sre@nimbushealth.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Date: 2025-05-13T11:02:00-07:00
Subject: Re: SLO cadence & degradation margin (p50/p95) — Nimbus Health

Hi Danielle,

Really helpful questions — appreciate the clarity. I pulled together a short proposal (attached) and summarized the practical tradeoffs below. High level: we can structure the contractual measurement to avoid noisy credit triggers while preserving a meaningful latency commitment.

Proposal (summary):
1) Measurement cadence: define a primary measurement "epoch" of 12 hours. For contractual p50/p95 commitments we calculate latency percentiles per-epoch and then evaluate a 30-day compliance window as the fraction of epochs meeting the target.
   - Example: p95 target = 350ms. If 27 of 60 epochs in the 30-day window meet p95 <= 350ms, that counts toward compliance based on the agreed aggregation rule (we propose a 90% epoch-compliance requirement).
2) Transient degradation margin (carveout): allow automatic carveouts for epochs where traffic exceeds a pre-agreed burst threshold (e.g., >3x baseline TPS or sustained traffic > X rps for >10 minutes). These carveouts are limited to a small fraction of epochs per rolling 90-day period (we propose max 3 carveouts / 90 days).
3) Short outage handling and credit calc: SLA credits triggered only when the number of non-compliant epochs exceeds the contractual tolerance. Single-day spikes would not automatically create credits unless they push epoch non-compliance past the tolerance.
4) Fallback / mitigation: when epochs are non-compliant we automatically route to pre-defined fallback model variants (lower-latency quantized variant) for the remainder of the epoch to protect downstream UX; we track these fallbacks in the console.

Operational implications:
- Pros: epoch-based measurement prevents a single noisy call from moving long-term percentiles; carveouts protect customer from known burst patterns; epochs are simple to audit.
- Cons: epochs introduce quantization (a 12hr bad epoch still counts even if most minutes were fine), so we pair epochs with short-term mitigations and an explicit carveout process.

Attached: slo_epoch_proposal_v1.pdf (includes examples, math, and suggested contract language) and slo_fallback_runbook.md.

Can you share what baseline TPS Nimbus expects for the hosted endpoints (typical rps and peak factor)? Once we have that we can propose concrete threshold numbers. If you're comfortable, we can include this epoch-plus-carveout language in the draft addendum and limit carveouts to a small number of epochs per quarter.

Next steps:
- You: confirm baseline TPS and whether 12hr epochs are acceptable.
- Us: draft amendment language and a runbook for carveout approval + audit trail.

Thanks,

Karthik Iyer
Head of Sales Engineering | Redwood Inference
karthik_iyer@redwood.com
Attachment: slo_epoch_proposal_v1.pdf; slo_fallback_runbook.md

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>
Cc: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com>
Date: 2025-05-14T08:27:00-07:00
Subject: Internal: Nimbus SLO cadence proposal — approval ask

Ben / Lauren — quick heads-up on a proposed SLO framing for Nimbus Health.

Context: Nimbus asked whether we can avoid noisy p95 credit triggers caused by short-lived regional bursts. I proposed a 12hr-epoch measurement with a limited transient carveout (max 3 carveouts / 90 days) and automated fallbacks to quantized model variants when epochs degrade.

Ask:
- Sales: ok to offer epoch-based measurement + 3 carveouts? Is that permissible for enterprise deals in the US region?
- Finance / Legal: are we comfortable with the credit calc being epoch-count based (credits only when non-compliant epochs exceed tolerance) rather than direct rolling quantile recomputation?

Notes for consideration:
- This is more conservative for us than a pure rolling-window p95, because a 12hr bad window still counts; carveouts limit liability for true spikes.
- We need Legal to sign-off on carveout auditability: each carveout must have a short justification and telemetry snapshot (traffic heatmap + KV cache state) to be eligible.

If you want, I can tighten the carveout definition to a specific rps multiplier and only allow carveouts for regional bursts that match a documented incident timeline.

Thanks,
Karthik

On a separate note: if we proceed, we should include the fallback variant name and quantization delta in the amendment so the customer knows the UX tradeoff when fallbacks kick in.

From: Danielle Ortiz <dani.ortiz@nimbushealth.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Cc: Nimbus Health SRE <sre@nimbushealth.com>
Date: 2025-05-16T16:42:00-07:00
Subject: Re: SLO cadence & degradation margin (p50/p95) — Nimbus Health

Karthik,

Thanks — that proposal is very helpful and addresses our concerns. A few clarifying points from SRE/legal:
- 12hr epochs are acceptable to us as long as the carveout criteria are explicit. Please propose a numeric threshold (we suggested 3x baseline rps earlier).
- We prefer carveouts to be limited per 90-day rolling window and require an audit artifact (console snapshot + short incident note). Agree that 3 carveouts / 90 days is a reasonable starting point.
- For the fallback, please include the fallback variant name and estimated latency delta in the amendment (we want to set customer-facing expectations).
- For SLA credits: Nimbus requests that credits only be applied when >5% of epochs in a 30-day window are non-compliant (so credits are not triggered by isolated spikes).

If you can send back the amendment language with the numeric thresholds and fallback variant, Legal will fast-track review. Once that's in contract we can sign and move to pilot.

Appreciate the responsiveness.

— Danielle Ortiz
Sr. Manager, Platform Engineering
Nimbus Health
